summary: Erich Frauwallner was an Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Vienna (1918–1921). He held various posts at Vienna, serving as director (1938, 1942) and professor (1955–1964), and edited the WZKS (ca. 1957–1974).

Erich Haenisch specialized in Sinology and Iranian and Central Asian studies, studying at Humboldt University of Berlin under Wilhelm Grube. He held professorships at Göttingen (1925), Leipzig (ca. 1925–1932), Berlin (1932), and Munich (1927–1951).

Erich Heintel was a philosopher who earned his doctorate (ca. 1930–1936) and completed his habilitation (1940) at the University of Vienna. He served there as extraordinary professor (1952) and ordinary professor of philosophy (1960–1982).

Erich Rudolf Jaensch was a philosopher who studied at Breslau, Göttingen (PhD 1905–1909), and Strasbourg. He served as professor of philosophy at the University of Halle-Wittenberg (1912–1913) and as ordinary professor at the University of Marburg from 1913.

Erik Braun is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who studied at Harvard University under Janet Gyatso, Jonathan Evans, John Okell, and Saw Tun. He is attested on the faculty at the University of Virginia in 2026.

Erik Haarh was a Tibetology and linguistics scholar who earned his doctorate from the University of Copenhagen (attested 1969). He worked at the Royal Danish Library (1956–1962) and served as a department head and professor at Aarhus University (1969, 1983).

Erik J. Hammerstrom is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned his PhD from Indiana University Bloomington (attested 2010) and served as assistant professor of religion at Pacific Lutheran University (attested 2016).
Erik Pema Kunsang is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies figure who has served as director of Rangjung Yeshe Publications (from ca. 1981) and as a resident teacher at Rangjung Yeshe Gomde Denmark.

Erik Zürcher was a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD at Leiden University, also studying under Paul Demiéville, Prabodh Chandra Bagchi, and J. J. L. Duyvendak. He directed Leiden University (1961–1993) and co-edited T'oung Pao (1975–1992).

Erik-Jan Zürcher is a historian and linguist who completed his BA and PhD at Leiden University. He held positions at Radboud University Nijmegen (1977–1997), the International Institute of Social History (1990–1999, 2008–2012), and Leiden University (from 1997).

Erling von Mende is a Sinologist who studied at Hamburg, Freiburg, Bonn, and Cologne (PhD 1964–1969, habilitation by 1979). He served as professor of Sinology at the Free University of Berlin from 1983 to 2007.
Ernest Arthur Gardner was an archaeologist and historian who studied at Gonville and Caius College from ca. 1880 to 1884. He later held a post at the University of London from 1924 to 1926.

Ernest Bender was an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied at Temple University and the University of Pennsylvania under W. Norman Brown, Zellig S. Harris, and Henry Hoenigswald. He taught at the University of Pennsylvania as professor from 1950 to 1989.

Ernest Fenollosa was a philosopher, Japanologist, and historian who studied at Harvard and the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston. He taught at the University of Tokyo (1878) and served as curator of the Oriental Collection at the MFA Boston (1890–1896).

Ernest John Henry Mackay was a scholar of archaeology and Indology who earned his BA, MA, and DLitt at the University of Bristol. He served as Custodian of Antiquities for the Government of Palestine from 1919 to 1922.

Ernest Renan worked in religious studies, linguistics, and archaeology, studying under Eugène Burnouf and Étienne Marc Quatremère at the Collège de France. He held posts at the Bibliothèque nationale de France (1851–1860) and the Collège de France (from 1861).

Ernest Sosa is a philosopher who studied at the University of Miami and the University of Pittsburgh under Roderick M. Chisholm. He served as professor at Brown University starting in 1964 and at Rutgers University from 1998 to 2006.

Ernst Curtius was an archaeologist and historian who studied at Bonn and Göttingen under Friedrich Gottlieb Welcker and Christian August Brandis. He held professorships at Berlin (from 1844) and Göttingen (1855–1867), and directed the Altes Museum (ca. 1868–1896).

Ernst Förstemann worked in linguistics and history, studying at Berlin and Halle-Wittenberg under August Friedrich Pott, Karl Lachmann, and Franz Bopp. He served as librarian at the Stolberg-Wernigerode library (1851) and head of the Dresden library (1865–1887).

Ernst Fürlinger is a scholar of religious studies, Indology, and philosophy who habilitated at the University of Vienna (2013). He held posts at St. Virgil Salzburg (1991–2001), Vienna (2006–2016), and the University for Continuing Education Krems (2007–2023).
